source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx:
【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. UCE on Primary, CE on Secondary specific BIOS setup : • Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration > — Mirror Mode = Full Mirror Mode • Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > — Enforce Population POR = Disable • Disabling this knob is not required but was disabled because a non-POR memory population was used. It is highly recommended to have a POR memory population. 2. Complete steps 1-6 in the CE recipe to check on the state of the system, find an address to inject to, and to unlock the injectors. 3. Using the desired target address, arm the injectors on the secondary channel for acorrectable ECC error and do not inject or consume. >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(addr=0x000100000000, errType="ce", immInject=False, immConsume=False, Inj2ndCh=True, verbose=True, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False) 4. Using the desired target address, arm the injectors on the primary channel for an uncorrectable ECC error and do not inject or consume. The order of this step and the previous step does not matter. >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(addr=0x000100000000, errType="uce", immInject=False, immConsume=False, Inj2ndCh=False, verbose=True, showErrorRegs=True, checkEInjLock=False) 5. Check the state of the memory error injectors to verify that they are armed as expected. For this particular target address, the primary channel is {socket 0, mc 0, channel 0 (only 1 channel per IMC so redundant)} and it's shown that the injector is armed for a multi-device ECC error which is uncorrectable. Also shown is the injector on the secondary channel (mc 1) which is armed for a single device single bit ECC error which is correctable. >>> ei.mem.showMemInjectors(socket=0) 6. Write to the target address. 0xcafecafecafecafe was chosen as an example. >>> itp.threads[0].mem("0x000100000000p", 8, 0xcafecafecafecafe) 7. Write back invalidate all the caches so modified cachelines will be written back toDDR5 memory. This action will inject the errors to memory. >>> itp.threads[0].wbinvd() 8. Check that the memory error injectors are now unarmed since the write back invalidate injected the errors. >>> ei.mem.showMemInjectors(socket=0) 9. Read the target address to consume the errors. The primary data will be read first, an uncorrectable ECC error will be detected, secondary (mirrored) data will be read, a correctable ECC error will be detected, corrected, logged, mirror scrub and check on the primary channel will occur, and the good data will be delivered to the requester. >>> itp.threads[0].mem('0x000100000000p', 8) 10. Check the primary channel's B2CMI MCA bank. There should be a valid (valid==1) corrected (uc==0) MCA error indicating a read ECC error (mscod==1) with a corrected error count (corrcount) of 1. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_status_shadow >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_status_shadow.showfields()
 11. Primary B2CMI's MCi_ADDR should match the target address. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_addr_shadow 12. Primary B2CMI's MCi_MISC should indicate that the following: error was corrected during mirroring and mirror scrub was successful (mirrorcorrerr==1), transaction was to a mirrored region (mccmdmirrregion==1), mccmdvld==1 to indicate the other mccmd fields are valid, mirror scrub check read returned good data (errortype[3]==1), and the transaction couldn't be corrected by ECC (errortype[2]==1). >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_misc_shadow >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mci_misc_shadow.showfields()
 13. The secondary channel's IMC should have a valid (valid==1) corrected (UC==0) MCA error indicating that there was a corrected demand read ECC error (mscod==0x80) with a corrected error count (corrcount) of 1. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc_status_shadow >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc_status_shadow.showfields()
 14. Secondary IMC's MCi_ADDR should match the target address. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc8_addr_shadow 15. Secondary IMC's MCi_MISC contains FRU identification details which are also logged in the retry read error logs. See the processor register specification for the decoding of IMC MCi_MISC. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.imc0_mc_misc_shadow 16. Secondary IMC's retry read error logs configured to log demand read ECC errors should have valid data. Not going into fine detail here about what to expect because there's another recipe that goes into detail about what to expect in the case of a corrected ECC error and the register definitions should be clear. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log[1] >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log[1].showfields()
 >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address1[1] >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address1[1].showfields()
 >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address2[1] >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address2[1].showfields()
 >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_address3[1] >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.mc1.ch0.mcchan.retry_rd_err_log_parity[1] 17. Resume the system to allow all error handling flows to complete. >>> go()

source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- UCE on Primary, CE on Secondary (Intel full mirror UCE on Primary, CE on Secondary error injection): requires CScripts/EDKII unlock (Lock Chipset=Disable, MSR Lock Control=Disable, EV DFX Features=Enable, WHEA Error Injection Support=Enable) + the user/FAE to drive the Cscript/error-injection harness for this exact pattern. Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'mirror|primary|corrected|uncorrected'; echo __full_mirror_UCE_on_Primary,_CE_on_Secondary; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".

disposition_reason: The experiment depends on ordering and locality: both injectors must be armed before writeback, writeback must place each fault into its mapped copy, and the later read must first encounter the primary UCE then recover data from the secondary CE. Primary MSCOD1 plus mirror misc bits proves mirror recovery; secondary MSCOD0x80 and retry logs prove correction of the buddy copy. Without the armed/unarmed transitions or address equality, those records could be unrelated. A repeat would add ambiguous errors. test_case.purpose: Prove Full-Mirror recovery when the primary copy has a UCE and the secondary copy has a CE at the same cache line, delivering corrected data while recording both primary mirror handling and secondary corrected-read detail.
required_package: CScripts and ITP versions/hashes/licenses plus CE-recipe dependency
Address0x100000000 primary socket0/MC0/ch0 and secondary MC1 mapping
Approved injector masks/roles and exact primary B2CMI/secondary IMC/retry field oracle
Dedicated window, memory-content approval, serial/OOB recovery and restoration
test_case.test_command: Validate Full-Mirror topology and address mapping through the referenced CE recipe; preserve register/log baselines; arm secondary CE with Inj2ndCh=True and primary UCE with Inj2ndCh=False, both deferred; verify socket0 injectors; write the exact example value, wbinvd, verify disarm and read the same address; confirm primary B2CMI valid/uc/mscod/corrcount/address/misc fields and secondary IMC valid/UC/MSCOD0x80/count/address/FRU plus retry-read records; go once, collect health and restore.
